input.text: Across from the Temple of Heaven's east gate stands an eight-floor building with a glittering specialty: Hongqiao Market — known worldwide as Beijing's Pearl Market, and called by China's own gem trade "the First House of Pearls in the Capital." Floors three to five are wall-to-wall pearls — freshwater strands from a few dollars, saltwater specimens in velvet cases, plus gold, jade, and silk on the other floors. The truth-in-shopping rules of Beijing markets apply doubly for pearls: trust your eyes, ask for certificates on the big purchases, and know that bargaining is expected from the very first quote. Even if you buy nothing, come at mid-morning when the traders are cheerful and the aisles perform their orchestra of offers. Then walk straight into the Temple of Heaven opposite — prayer first, pearls after — the most Beijing pairing of the sacred and the retail.
